clue.text: It holds personalities with first half-second

indicators.note: the front half of the word is told to take second place, so the two halves swap round

blocks.note: your self is your personality, so personalities are selves

explanation.surface: Something that contains famous personalities, timed to the first half-second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First half-second' reads as a tiny moment of time but tells you to move the front half of the word behind the back half. This answer is the theme: every '1 across' in the puzzle means a boat or ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is any container such as a jug or bowl, something made to hold liquid.

clue.text: Said to be the top level in those leading religious authority

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is matched by its sound
one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: the attic is the top floor of a house
the van is the front of an army, those leading

explanation.surface: Someone claimed to be at the top level among leaders of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The van is the front rank of an army, so 'those leading' fits it; the homophone is only approximate, which older puzzles allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican, the papal seat in Rome, stands for the governing authority of the Roman Catholic Church.

blocks.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
a horn is a bony outgrowth on an animal's head

explanation.surface: Trimming the tip of a growth.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' puts S above HORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorn is the past participle of shear, so it means clipped as sheep's wool is.

clue.text: Hair-raising! The Spanish were ahead with a smooth finish

indicators.note: in a down answer raising something lifts it so it reads from the bottom up

blocks.note: a mane is a long head of hair
el is Spanish for the
those who led were ahead

explanation.surface: A thrilling moment as Spain led, with a polished end.
explanation.walkthrough: MANE raised in a down answer gives ENAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamelled means coated with a hard glossy layer, giving the surface a smooth glazed coat.

blocks.note: to mud something is to make it dirty, and a cow is a beast

explanation.surface: Someone who gets an animal filthy, likened to a container.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb phrase 'makes dirty' wraps round its object 'beast', so the wordplay reads MUDS (makes dirty) then COW (beast).
explanation.definitionFit: A mud scow is a flat-bottomed barge used to carry dredged mud, so it is a kind of boat.

blocks.note: a mart is a market or fair
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Giving a swallow a fair chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A martlet is an old word for a house martin or swift, birds of the swallow kind.

clue.text: Went underground to come up for the first time

definitions.text: come up for the first time

indicators.note: in a down answer coming up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to tube is to travel on the London Underground, the Tube

explanation.surface: Someone who travelled on the Tube emerges for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come up' does double duty, turning the word round and starting the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To debut is to make a first public appearance, to emerge into view for the first time.

clue.text: Diver gives expression of surprise at short time to go on

blocks.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
a mo is a moment
to rant is to go on and on

explanation.surface: A diver gasps at having little time left to continue.
explanation.definitionFit: The cormorant is a seabird that dives underwater to catch fish.

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tribute to someone killed in war.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a wreath is laid for a fallen soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreaths of flowers or poppies are laid at memorials to honour those killed in battle.

blocks.note: first meaning: main, chief
second meaning: a wire clip that joins papers

explanation.definitionFit: Staple as an adjective means chief or basic, and as a noun names a bent wire clip for holding sheets together.

indicators.note: a horse that rears goes up on its back legs, so the word is turned round
one word is placed inside the other

blocks.note: to mow is to crop grass
a taster is a small sample

explanation.surface: Farm produce raised as a small trial batch.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'reared' cannot mean upwards, so it simply means turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-master is a sailing ship with two masts, so it is a kind of vessel.

blocks.note: first meaning: to ... into someone is to bump into them
second meaning: a flat-bottomed boat used on rivers and canals

explanation.walkthrough: The verb is used with 'into', just as the definition is: to barge into is to bump into.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as a verb for colliding clumsily and as a noun for a cargo boat on canals.

indicators.note: something going has gone off or broken up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether a craft could cross the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits a joke: a canoe is hardly an ocean-going craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light narrow boat paddled by hand, a small kind of vessel.

indicators.note: the outer word holds the others within it

blocks.note: a pit is a hole in the ground
the lot means the whole thing
a boa is a large snake

explanation.surface: An entire snake pit holding a container.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'snake-pit' disguises the break between two separate pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot boat carries harbour pilots out to ships needing guidance, so it is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: In France she's able to overturn obsolete little 1 across

indicators.note: turning something over puts it the other way round

blocks.note: to be able is to be capable, one who can
elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A French woman is capable of capsizing an old small craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obsolete' is fair because today the word means an engine housing or a balloon's basket; the boat sense is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacelle once meant a small boat, an old sense now replaced by the engine housing or balloon basket.

clue.text: One who does 4 to air differences causes discord

indicators.note: differences suggest something made different, so the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: a char is a cleaner, one who does the housework
IV is 4 in Roman numerals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleaner airing grievances stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The 4 looks like a reference to 4-down or 4-across, but it is just the number. A char is a British cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a noisy mock serenade of pans and kettles, so a din or cacophony.

blocks.note: first meaning: the woollen cloth woven in a Scottish clan check pattern
second meaning: a single-masted sailing boat of the Mediterranean

explanation.walkthrough: 'Check design of' reads like a pattern on a container; the two meanings are unrelated.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan is the plaid pattern of Highland dress and also the name of a small lateen-rigged Mediterranean coaster.

clue.text: Put back to control civil power?

blocks.note: to rein in is to control
the state is the civil power of government

explanation.surface: Restoring someone to keep governmental power in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone to a former position, returning them to it.

blocks.note: first meaning: a shoe made of a sole held on by straps
second meaning: a long narrow boat used in the Levant

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition describes the shoe rather than naming it, which is fair because that is exactly what it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Open summer footwear is a sole fastened with straps, and the same word names an eastern Mediterranean boat.

clue.text: Free to include king bearing gander

indicators.note: including something takes it inside

blocks.note: loose means free
K is the chess abbreviation for king
east, a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Releasing a king who carries a goose.
explanation.walkthrough: K goes inside LOOSE, then E follows. 'Gander' is not the goose but slang for a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a gander is informal for having a look, and a look-see is likewise a quick inspection.

indicators.note: a capsized boat is turned upside down, so this word is turned round
one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: the Red Sea
a rift is a break or breach

explanation.surface: A gap opens in the sea and a ship overturns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea' names a particular sea by its colour; capsizing turns it round before the break goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is a fishing boat that uses drift nets, so it is a kind of vessel.

indicators.note: drawing an outline goes round the edges of something, enclosing it

blocks.note: to dub is to name
taken as written
E for eastern

explanation.surface: Naming a flower from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword's thing that flows, a river, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube is one of Europe's great rivers, and a flower in crossword sense is anything that flows.

indicators.note: sound here means as heard, so the word matches by pronunciation

blocks.note: to pleat is to tuck cloth, so again is re-pleat

explanation.surface: Stuffed with good food, eating again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full of sound' reads as one phrase, but 'Full' alone is the definition. Tuck is British slang for food, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means well fed, having eaten as much as one can.

blocks.note: first meaning: something that balances another, a counterweight
second meaning: set off to one side, misaligned

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a complaint about pay; the two meanings are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: An offset balances a loss, and something offset is displaced sideways from its proper position.

clue.text: Day with idiot around at 1 across

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: Fri is short for Friday
a goon is a fool
taken as written

explanation.surface: A day spent with a fool at a container.
explanation.walkthrough: The days of the week have standard three-letter abbreviations, used freely in wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigatoon is a small square-sterned Venetian sailing vessel, an obscure kind of ship.

clue.text: Joint has no right to give continual pain

indicators.note: having none of something means it is taken away

blocks.note: a grievance that rankles keeps hurting
R for right

explanation.surface: An aching joint gives constant pain.
explanation.walkthrough: RANKLE loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the hinge where foot meets leg, one of the body's joints.

clue.text: 1 across from the right bits of water

indicators.note: in an across answer, reading from the right means reading backwards

blocks.note: pools are small areas of water

explanation.surface: A container taken from small patches of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a single-masted sailing boat, so it is a kind of vessel.

indicators.note: the content of the phrase is what lies inside it

blocks.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: A poet's early years were genuinely happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like an adjective, happy, but signals the letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An odist is a writer of odes, lyric poems of praise, and so a kind of poet.

blocks.note: first meaning: a single-masted fishing boat
second meaning: a sharp slap

explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing a blow' sounds like a sailing ship waiting for wind; the two meanings are unrelated.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a small coastal fishing boat, and also a hard slap with the open hand.

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: a bus is a vehicle
a Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A cheerful vehicle coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective but is the sailors' nickname for a Royal Marine, a British naval soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine is a warship that travels under water, so it is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Soundly strain with many sheets in 1 across

indicators.note: soundly here means by sound, so the words are judged as spoken

blocks.note: to strain is to try hard
a ream is 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Pulling hard with lots of sails on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, TRY and REAM give TRIREME. 'Sheets' also suggests sails, which fits the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme is an ancient Greek or Roman warship with three banks of oars, so it is a kind of vessel.

blocks.note: first meaning: a lateen-rigged Mediterranean sailing ship
second meaning: a long seat with a back, for two or more

explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' looks like a reversal signal for the vessel, but it is part of the second definition: a seat with a back.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a sofa, a long upholstered seat with a back, and also an old two-masted Mediterranean ship.
